body.statement:
Let \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_J\) be finite nonnegative measures and let
\(\lambda=\sum_{j=1}^J\lambda_j\).  There are measurable functions
\(f_j\ge0\) such that \(d\lambda_j=f_jd\lambda\) and
\(\sum_{j=1}^Jf_j=1\), \(\lambda\)-almost everywhere.

source.locator: Halmos, Measure Theory, Radon--Nikodym theorem, specialized to a finite dominating sum
source.verbatim_statement: If (X,S,mu) is a totally sigma-finite measure space and if a sigma-finite signed measure nu on S is absolutely continuous with respect to mu, then there exists a finite valued measurable function f on X such that nu(E) = integral_E f dmu for every measurable set E.

attestation.note: Halmos, Measure Theory, Section 31, Theorem B, pp. 128-129; transcription checked from a scan on 2026-09-13. The finite-family node follows by applying the theorem to each lambda_j against their finite sum.

body.justification: The reverse construction needs simultaneous measurable densities with respect to one dominating probability measure.
body.consumer: It makes the initial and feedback kernels measurable and normalized.
